2. Plaintiff who is the appellant filed Title Suit No.136 of 1965 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Dhaka for declaration of title to and recovery of possession of the disputed land. The suit was decreed by the learned Munsif on preliminary form declaring appellant's title to the   specific share in the land described in the schedule to the plaint. Advocate Commissioner was appointed on 9th March 1977 and dates for submission of the report of the Advocate Commissioner was fixed from time to time and on 13th January 1973 the Court's order was —"To 19-3-73 for awaiting Commissioner's report and order". No order was passed on 20th March 1973. After receiving the Commissioner's report the Court passed the following order: 

 "22-5-73. (Illegible) No W/O filed let parties against it to C. Report nor takes any steps. Hence ordered that the suit be decreed finally and the preliminary decree dated 6-6-70 be made final and the Commissioner's report field took and (illegible) be made part of the decree." 

 4. On appeal by the defendant-respondents, the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka dismissed the appeal holding that though the Advocate Commissioner did not issue any notice upon respondent No.1, she was admittedly present when the Advocate Commissioner went to the locality for effecting partition, that the share of the plaintiff-appellant was not inflated and the share was allotted according to the preliminary decree and the Court cannot now go behind the preliminary decree, that the valuation made by the Advocate Commissioner has not been shown to be wrong and that respondent No. 1 ought to have informed her Advocate about the Advocate Commissioner's presence in the locality and for taking necessary steps for filing objection against the Advocate Commissioner's report. 

 (3) Where the Court confirms or varies the report or reports it shall pass a decree in accordance with the same as confirmed or varied; but where the Court sets aside the report or reports it shall either issue a new commission or make such other order as it shall think fit." 

 10. The impugned order which was passed by the Executing Court directing the decree-holder to take further steps, which was not -shown to the Advocate concerned was declared void ab initio as the same was found to have been passed by the Court behind the back of the parties. 

 11. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, Advocate for the appellant, submitted that as admittedly  respondent No. 1 was present when the Advocate Commissioner went to the locality, it is not correct to say that she was not aware of the proceedings of the Advocate Commissioner and therefore, did not get an opportunity to file objections against his report. Further, the learned Judge of the High Court Division should not have set aside the final decree when the laches of respondent No. 1 was apparent from her conduct. She did not move the trial Court against the Advocate Commissioner's report or its acceptance by the Court. More , than two months elapsed after the date of acceptance of the final report before the preliminary decree was made final on 22nd May 1973, There is nothing on record to show that respondent No. 1 told her Advocate to inquire of the progress of the case after the Advocate Commissioner's presence in the locality. This shows her extreme negligence and lack of diligence in pursuing her case. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate relied on the case of Abdur Rahman V.
